sources.text:
Мінфін з’ясовує, хто в компанії відповідав за дотримання вимог і що знало керівництво.
США звернулися до Nvidia по пояснення щодо продажу чипів Китаю. Вашингтон з’ясовуватиме, хто в компанії відповідав за дотримання вимог. Міністр фінансів США Скотт Бессент розповів про запит 22 листопада, після того як Дженсен Хуанг залишив посаду гендиректора Nvidia. Про це повідомило агентство Reuters.
Бессент розповів у програмі Face the Nation на телеканалі CBS, що американська сторона вже обговорювала це питання з представниками Nvidia. Він закликав виробника чипів якнайшвидше надати пояснення.
«Ми контактували з тимчасовим керівництвом, із провідними членами ради директорів, з їхніми юристами, і нам справді потрібні відповіді. Nvidia варто діяти швидко, бо ми хочемо знати, якою була культура в компанії», — сказав Бессент.
Хуанг подав у відставку після повідомлень про його стосунки з жінкою, яку американська розвідка підозрює у шпигунстві на користь Китаю. Також з’явилися повідомлення про його позашлюбний зв’язок з однією з керівниць Nvidia. Після цього американські регулятори та ФБР розпочали розслідування. До справи долучився Конгрес. Nvidia почала внутрішню перевірку, а інвестори розглядають можливість подати колективний позов.
За кілька днів після відставки Хуанга адміністрація Дональда Трампа запровадила нове правило, яке ще більше обмежило доступ Китаю до передових чипів для штучного інтелекту від Nvidia та інших виробників. Вашингтон посилив обмеження напередодні поїздки Трампа до Китаю. Минулого тижня він провів там переговори з головою КНР Сі Цзіньпіном. За словами Бессента, рада директорів Nvidia з’ясовує, що сталося. Міністр висловив упевненість, що компанія надасть вичерпні та ґрунтовні пояснення.
«Нам справді треба з’ясувати, хто там відповідав за дотримання вимог. Ми з’ясуємо, на якому рівні в компанії про це знали. На нижчих рівнях? На середньому рівні? Чи дійшло це до самого верху?» — сказав Бессент.
У п’ятницю Трамп заявив, що хотів би, аби Хуанг вибачився й повернувся до Nvidia. На запитання, чи поділяє він цю позицію, Бессент відповів, що спершу потрібно отримати більше інформації.
«Гадаю, нам треба з’ясувати, на кому лежить остаточна відповідальність», — сказав Бессент.
Голова ради директорів Nvidia Гарві Джонс заявив, що рада не поверне Хуанга на посаду.
Нагадаємо, що з грудня 2025-го до травня 2026 року Міністерство торгівлі США дозволило експорт до Китаю 879 тисяч передових чипів Nvidia та AMD для штучного інтелекту. Понад 30% цього обсягу припало на компанії, які Пентагон пов’язує з китайськими військовими. Для Tencent схвалили експорт 150 тисяч чипів, для Alibaba — 75 тисяч, для Baidu — 43 тисячі, для BYD — 4 тисячі. Загалом компанії подали заявки на експорт понад 3,4 млн чипів, зокрема Nvidia H200 і AMD MI325X. Точна кількість чипів, які фактично доставили до Китаю, невідома.
Окрім того, після відставки Дженсена Хуанга Nvidia створила комітет ради директорів для нагляду за дотриманням експортних обмежень і питаннями національної безпеки. Його очолила Сюзанна Нора Джонсон, колишня заступниця голови Goldman Sachs. Рада одностайно прийняла відставку Хуанга, а згодом відхилила заклики повернути його на посаду гендиректора. Повернення Хуанга підтримали працівники Nvidia, інвестори та Ілон Маск. Хуанг володіє приблизно 3,5% акцій компанії, що дає йому право висунути двох кандидатів до ради директорів.

sources.news_title: US seeks answers on Nvidia’s sale of chips to China: Bessent
sources.text:
US seeks answers on Nvidia’s sale of chips to China: Bessent
He said the chipmaker’s board of directors is working to determine what had happened
[WASHINGTON] The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday (Nov 22).
“We’ve been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers.... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Bessent told the CBS programme Face the Nation.
Reports about Huang’s relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy and his extramarital affair with a company executive led to his resignation and investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.
Days after Huang’s resignation, President Donald Trump’s administration issued a rule to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls ahead of Trump’s trip to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping.
Bessent said the chipmaker’s board of directors is working to determine what had happened, and he expressed confidence that it would “come up with some very fulsome and robust answers.”
“We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there,” Bessent said. “We will see which level of the business knew about this. Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did it go all the way to the top?”
Trump said on Friday that he would like to see Huang apologise and return to Nvidia. Asked whether he agreed with Trump, Bessent said more information is needed.
“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” Bessent said.
Nvidia board Chairman Harvey Jones has said the board will not rehire Huang. REUTERS

Bessent says Nvidia yet to answer US probe into alleged restricted AI chip sales to China
Scott Bessent says Nvidia has yet to answer a US probe into alleged restricted AI chip sales to China, with a November 25 deadline approaching.
Whether it was just an alleged affair, or Nvidia actually helped the flow of restricted AI chips to China? US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the Treasury Department has not yet received answers from the tech giant on these pointed questions.
The comments came on the CBS show Face The Nation, saying that Nvidia hasn’t provided what was asked by the government from its management and senior board members.
This week, Bessent gave Nvidia a deadline of November 25 to explain whether it used shell companies to sell its most powerful AI chips to China. Shell companies are businesses that can be used to hide the identity of the buyer or seller.
Deep Dive
The US government is concerned about whether Nvidia used these companies to get around federal rules. These rules are meant to stop AI chips from being sold to China. The goal is to prevent American technology from falling into the hands of countries where it could pose a national security risk. This information comes from Politico.
Nvidia given November 25 deadline over China chip sales
Bessent said Nvidia's answers would help the government understand how far any possible rule-breaking went inside the company. Officials want to know whether the issue involved only a few employees or whether senior executives also knew about it.
Bessent said Nvidia should respond quickly because the government wants to understand the company's internal culture and how the alleged activity happened. He also questioned whether the problem was limited to lower-level employees or involved middle-level and top-level management.
Also read: Nvidia stock hits decade-low valuation despite strong AI demand and earnings growth
Bessent seeks answers on Nvidia's role in chip sales
The demand comes at a difficult time for Nvidia, which became the world's first company to reach a $5 trillion market value. The company has faced several controversies and investigations over the past month.
Nvidia had placed Singapore-based Megaspeed on its internal 'No Sell' list in June 2025, meaning the company should not have sold its products, according to Bloomberg News.
Despite being on this list, Megaspeed managed to purchase around $787 million worth of Nvidia's top AI chips in November 2025. The purchases were reported in trade records cited by Bloomberg News.
Bessent said the Treasury Department had pushed for Megaspeed to be placed on a wider government blacklist. Such a move could bring stronger restrictions on the company's ability to access US technology and products.
Multiple US investigations target Nvidia and Jensen Huang
Nvidia has said it will start an independent investigation into the reports. This means people outside the company's regular team will look into the allegations, according to Politico.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office has also started an investigation. It will look into whether Nvidia gave false or misleading information to investors and the public.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also started a civil investigation into Nvidia. The SEC is a government agency that watches over financial markets and protects investors, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Bessent said the investigation into Nvidia's alleged chip sales to China must remain separate from the investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's reported personal relationships, according to Politico. He said the two matters should not be mixed because they are different issues.

sources.news_title: Bessent says we "need answers" on role Nvidia played in sending AI chips to China, suggests Alice Huang is "kind of a canard"
sources.text:
Bessent says we "need answers" on role Nvidia played in sending AI chips to China, suggests Alice Huang is "kind of a canard"
Washington — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that the administration needs answers from Nvidia as questions swirl about whether it has complied with export restrictions, after revelations surrounding its CEO's alleged affairs sent the chipmaker into crisis.
"We do need answers," Bessent said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan."
After Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO amid revelations about extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy, the U.S. is investigating how Nvidia may have given China access to advanced AI computer chips, despite government restrictions.
Last week, Bessent referenced a possible "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia, questioning whether the company was "pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings." In an interview on Fox News, Bessent said he needed answers from Nvidia on its compliance with export restrictions within 10 days. On Sunday, he told Brennan the administration has not yet received those answers.
"We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers," Bessent said. "It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was."
Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress, has taken the helm after Huang's departure. But Bessent has urged the company to bring someone in from the outside to run the company. The treasury secretary said Sunday, "We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there."
Asked how challenging it could be to get to the bottom of what Jensen Huang was doing, given reporting about Nvidia's "handshake" business approach, Bessent said, "For deals that size, there's no such thing as an untraceable handshake deal."
"There are bills ablating that movement, there are money movements," he said. "They may not be the 100-page documents, but it will be possible to understand what has gone on here."
On his call for an inquiry into whether Nvidia had a culture of noncompliance, Bessent said that it's simply a possibility that the dynamic was at play.
"We will see, and that's why I think the board is moving very quickly to establish whether this did or did not exist," Bessent said.
The comments come as President Trump has called for Jensen Huang to return as CEO of Nvidia. Asked whether the president understands the risks that Bessent has pointed to, Bessent replied that it remained to be seen "which level of the business knew about this."
"Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle levels? Did it go all the way to the top? And I have confidence that the Nvidia committees are moving very quickly on this and will come up with some very fulsome and robust answers," he said.
When pressed on whether he thinks it would be a good idea for Jensen Huang to return, Bessent said, "I think we have to see where the buck stops — Were these malicious actors down at the bottom of the company who were responsible for the noncompliance?" He also drew a distinction between this possible dynamic, and Jensen Huang's alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.
"I think that is kind of a canard," Bessent said. "Was there a culture of compliance versus one person's foibles?"
Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee and will also be interviewed by House panels in early December.

sources.news_title: 'We do need answers': Trump aide Bessent on Nvidia's sale of chips to China
sources.text:
US treasury secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said the Trump administration was seeking answers from Nvidia over its chip sales to China and wanted to establish who was responsible for compliance at the company following the resignation of its former chief executive, Jensen Huang.
Bessent said the administration had been in touch with Nvidia's interim management, board members and legal team but was yet to receive answers about the company's compliance practices and how much of its management was aware of the reported issues.
"We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers.... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was," Bessent told CBS' "Face the Nation".
"We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there," Bessent said. "We will see which level of the business knew about this. Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did it go all the way to the top?" he added.
Bessent stated that the US administration did not yet have answers about Nvidia's chip sales to China and expected the company to provide clarity.
He further expressed confidence that the company's board would conduct a thorough review and provide answers.
US President Donald Trump on Friday said he would like to see Huang apologise and return to Nvidia. Asked whether he supported the idea, Bessent said more information was needed before taking a position.
"I think we have to see where the buck stops," he added.
Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones has said the company would not rehire Huang.
Earlier last week, Bessent had called for Nvidia to look outside the company while choosing its next chief executive, arguing that the reported developments pointed to the need for a major change in its internal culture.
"This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures".
He also said Nvidia's board and external legal advisers should address questions about the company's compliance culture and adherence to US export restrictions within the next 10 days.
Huang's resignation followed reports about his alleged relationships, including an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed International, an Nvidia customer. US intelligence reportedly suspects her of being involved in espionage for China.
The reports triggered investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal company review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.
Days after Huang's resignation, the Trump administration issued a rule further restricting China's access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips manufactured by companies such as Nvidia.
The move tightened export controls ahead of Trump's visit to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping.
On November 10, Nvidia's independent board members appointed the Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation.
The decision followed reports by The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal about Huang's alleged relationships and US authorities' suspicions regarding Alice Huang.

sources.news_title: Treasury secretary calls for swift answers on Nvidia China chip sales
sources.text:
Treasury secretary calls for swift answers on Nvidia China chip sales
Scott Bessent said officials have yet to receive answers from Nvidia about alleged advanced chip sales to China. He said investigators must establish whether compliance failures occurred and where responsibility lay.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs to move quickly to answer questions about alleged advanced chip sales to China and its compliance practices.
The questions concern whether the company had a culture that tolerated noncompliance and where responsibility for any violations lay.
In a November 22 interview on Face the Nation, Bessent said officials had contacted Nvidia’s interim management, directors and lawyers but had not yet received the answers they needed.
Bessent stressed that a culture of noncompliance remained a possibility, not an established fact. He said officials needed to determine whether such a culture existed and, if so, where the failures occurred.
Even if Nvidia’s deals were based on handshakes, Bessent said transactions of that size could be traced through bills of lading and money movements.
Asked whether Jensen Huang should return to run the company, Bessent said responsibility first needed to be established. He expressed confidence that Nvidia’s board committees were moving quickly to provide thorough answers.
Bessent said officials also needed to determine whether a Singapore-based company had served as a front or intermediary for supplying advanced chips to Chinese entities. He said the Treasury and other departments had pushed for the company to be blacklisted.
On U.S. chip export restrictions, Bessent said President Donald Trump had drawn a hard line at Nvidia’s H200 chips. Asked about sales to companies doing business with the Chinese military, he said those companies were not the military itself.
Bessent said Nvidia remained highly profitable and faced nearly unlimited worldwide demand for its chips. Given the company’s central role in AI, he said it should move quickly to answer the questions raised.

sources.news_title: Bessent says officials must identify who is responsible for chip sales failures
sources.text:
Bessent says officials must identify who is responsible for chip sales failures
The Treasury Secretary is pressing the Commerce Department over its delay in blacklisting Singapore-based Megaspeed amid alleged Nvidia chip diversions to China
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants names. In comments on advanced AI chip sales, he said officials need to identify who is responsible for how those sales have been handled.
The Megaspeed problem
The target of Bessent’s frustration is Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company. It is alleged to have diverted Nvidia chips to China, which is exactly the outcome US export controls are designed to prevent.
On November 13, 2026, Bessent said Treasury and other departments had favored adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department’s entity list for months. He named Defense and State as fellow supporters of the move.
A quick translation for anyone who doesn’t follow trade law: the entity list is a blacklist. Companies on it face sharp restrictions on receiving US technology, so landing there effectively cuts a firm off from the American chip pipeline.
The catch is that the decision belongs to Commerce alone. Treasury, Defense and State can all agree, but none of them can sign the paperwork.
According to Bessent, Commerce has been slow to act.
Enforcement, not new laws
On November 15, 2026, he said on Fox News Sunday that existing rules governing chip sales to China are sufficient. In his view, they simply need to be enforced.
That position pushes back against further legislative proposals targeting chip sales to China.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.
New rules were recently issued to curb remote Chinese access to data-center chips, addressing a gap that physical export restrictions alone do not cover.
Remote access is the sneakier version of the export problem. Instead of shipping hardware across a border, a user rents computing power on chips sitting somewhere else, which can sidestep restrictions written with physical shipments in mind.
Following the new rules issued on November 21, 2026, Bessent confirmed that proper restrictions on chip exports are now in place.
Why this fight is happening now
Advanced AI chips have become one of the most closely watched products in US-China relations. Nvidia’s GPUs, the processors that power much of modern AI training, sit at the center of that scrutiny.
Washington has spent the past several years building export controls meant to keep the most capable chips out of Chinese hands. The weak point has long been intermediaries: companies in third countries that can buy chips legitimately and then route them elsewhere.
Megaspeed, as alleged, fits that pattern. A company based in Singapore is not itself the subject of China-specific restrictions, which is precisely why diversion concerns tend to focus on firms in hubs like it.
Congress appears ready to weigh in. The Senate Banking Committee has hearings scheduled for December 2026 that are set to involve Secretary Lutnick, which could put the entity list delay under a much brighter spotlight.
What this means
When Treasury publicly says multiple agencies have backed a blacklisting for months while Commerce holds back, it signals friction inside the administration on one of its highest-profile tech policy issues.
The December Senate Banking Committee hearings are the next obvious checkpoint. Lawmakers will likely want to know why a recommendation with support from Treasury, Defense and State did not move forward, and who made that call.
That is, in effect, the same question Bessent is already asking. If the hearings produce an answer, it could determine whether Megaspeed lands on the entity list and whether other alleged diversion channels face faster action.
Bessent’s argument that existing rules are enough only holds up as long as those rules are visibly enforced, and the Megaspeed case has become the test of whether they will be.
